quote: Thus, we can consider 104.5 Hz ± 12.2 Hz as the flicker fusion frequency of dark-adapted female eyes being the mean ± SD of all calculated FFF values (Fig. 6).
note: Female FFF is similar to the male ventral eye region (the paper's abstract: temporal resolution of female eyes was similar to that of the ventral region of males) and significantly lower than the male dorsal region. Adults emerged in the lab from larvae collected at the Domini creek, northern Hungary; dark-adapted ERG preparations; flicker tested with LEDs at 372 nm (UV, about 1.2e15 photons/cm2/s) and 520 nm (green, about 2.0e15). The authors note that FFF rises with stimulus intensity and a light-adapted eye can be 40 to 70% higher, so dark-adapted values may underestimate temporal resolution during swarming. Main (desk-d164) holds the male dorsal eye value (148.7 Hz) and the spectral peaks from this paper; female and ventral FFF are not on main (grep by DOI and trait). Name matches main.
